No 1.0.0 gate is satisfied without current reproducible evidence or human review.

gates.title: Release commit has a clean working tree
Execution semantics are complete
gates.detail: Streaming, execution identity, idempotency and same-snapshot composition have current local evidence, including direct-actor, nested deadline/cancellation, telemetry-tree, stream-refusal, idempotency-isolation and adversarial-recursion checks; release review remains required.

gates.title: Performance budgets are enforced
gates.detail: docs/performance/budgets.json holds 15 calibrated limits covering dependency injection, policy evaluation, execution identity, idempotency, nested invocation, the ADR 0094 embedding boundary, complete stream lifecycle, compile and registration scaling, and compile memory. Budgets are ratios between scenarios measured in the same run and are enforced by scripts/check_performance_budgets.py in the CI Performance budgets job. V1-39 verified that only three historical calibration JSON records are preserved and recorded final-semantics coverage. V1-40 then preserved three current-semantic records and deliberately added embedding and registration/freeze limits with observed maxima. V1-41 makes the job run a deterministic artificial over-budget artifact through the same command-line checker before recording the real artifact; the checker rejects unsupported schemas, malformed values, missing or extra benchmark records, unbudgeted enforceable metrics, and execution-profile mismatches. The task branch's CI result is still required evidence, so this gate remains NEEDS_REVIEW. Runner behaviour and maintainer approval of every limit remain required.

gates.title: Interoperability conformance is demonstrated
gates.detail: ADR 0094 Version-pinned host fixtures include local Starlette 1.6.0, FastAPI 0.141.1, Django 6.1.1 and conditional Litestar 2.24.0 evidence. Task 30 audit validated lifecycle/context isolation under adversarial concurrent conditions, fail-closed auth, zero host object DI leakage, and idempotent cleanup across all host classes. The shared conformance harness in tests/conformance/test_host_harness.py runs across Standalone, Starlette, FastAPI, Django, and Litestar. tests/integration/test_framework_absence.py proves clean standalone/HTTP compilation, invocation and streaming in an isolated subprocess with all ecosystem frameworks blocked. The optional SQLAlchemy 2.0.54 SQLite fixture proves host-owned Session/commit/rollback; PostgreSQL is NOT RUN (conditional). OpenTelemetry SDK 1.44.0 export proves host trace integration and span isolation. No framework, ORM or exporter support claim follows. Maintainer review remains required.

gates.title: Security program is reviewed
gates.detail: V1-34 records the current 1.0 candidate threat boundary: authorization/principal, execution identity, direct/HTTP/MCP/embedded invocation, nested composition, idempotency, streaming/SSE, schema/persistence, documentation UIs, supply chain and telemetry. V1-35 then stabilized the authentication/authorization boundary and added tests/security/test_authority_boundary.py covering confused deputy, forged metadata claims, asserted subjects, credential objects offered as principals, cached discovery replay, confirmation-verifier failure and ambiguity, and cross-execution principal isolation. The adversarial review produced two findings, both fixed: S-1 (a streaming invocation silently discarded an idempotency selector) and S-2 (a handler could reassign the verified actor a nested child inherits, amplifying authority). Delegation remains unimplemented because RFC 0005 is Draft. A 2026-09-20 GitHub readback observed zero open Dependabot and secret-scanning alerts, while non-provider patterns and validity checks were disabled. V1-36 added the derandomized, bounded property and fuzz lanes in tests/property/, which found and fixed F-1 (a non-token request method escaped the dispatcher uncaught) and F-2 (request methods were uppercased, so post reached a POST route against RFC 9110 section 9.1). V1-37 closed the supply-chain evidence gaps: the release build generates a deterministic CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM describing the 7 built distributions with their real digests plus the locked runtime graph, verified by a separate checker (scripts/check_sbom.py); the recorded SHA256SUMS is re-verified by all 9 jobs that act on the bundle, including every PyPI upload; and the locked dependency audit is now a gate that build depends on, pinned to pip-audit 2.10.1 with --strict. A local dry run at 1.0.0.dev0 produced a byte-identical SBOM across two runs, matched all 14 artifact digests, and reported no known vulnerabilities. V1-38 independently reviewed 94ac5763386d8e18a78cbecd07cab227c42e6054 on 2026-09-21: the supported core, HTTP/ASGI/SSE, MCP, embedding, idempotency/composition, telemetry and CI/release boundaries were checked; 87 focused security/property tests passed; and the available GitHub readback returned no open CodeQL, Dependabot or secret-scanning alert. It found no unresolved P0/P1 in supported 1.0 scope. #469 tracks a non-blocking local-secret-inventory test-scope concern. Provenance and signing remain PEP 740 attestations produced by pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish under the workflow OIDC identity; Agnara holds no signing key. The live Trusted Publisher configuration, protected-environment reviewers and minted attestations are NEEDS CI: only an authorized release can establish them, and SECURITY.md holds the readback procedure. Those lanes are a regression net, not continuous fuzzing: no coverage-guided campaign, crash corpus, penetration test or concurrency/load test was performed; maintainer release review remains required. See docs/THREAT_MODEL.md sections 5 and 10 and docs/releases/1.0-release-rehearsal.md section 9.

gates.title: Public API is ready for stability
gates.detail: docs/releases/1.0-api-classification.md records V1-31: 166 stable canonical exports across 13 modules, 171 leaf-module aliases removed from the contract, DI moved to agnara.di, and the introspection snapshot field renamed to applications. Architecture tests and the installed-artifact gate import every stable name. Formal maintainer review and release CI remain required.

gates.title: Documentation reproduces supported applications
gates.detail: The earlier documentation-coverage audit found runnable examples for 9 of the 11 clean-room features and added telemetry/FastAPI examples. V1-42 adds tests/release/test_integrated_dogfooding.py: it builds all seven candidate wheels, installs them in a fresh Python 3.14 environment with index access closed for first-party artifacts, checks public imports, and runs compact standalone, SQLite/SQLAlchemy host, FastAPI embedded and FastAPI side-by-side consumers under python -I. This is reproducible local candidate evidence, not a support claim or a substitute for an independent clean-room reader, CI or maintainer review. See docs/releases/1.0-dogfooding.md.

gates.title: Publication workflow is rehearsed
gates.detail: V1-44 rehearsed the exact 4231617 candidate through a disposable 1.0.0 version transition: 14 artifacts for the 7 reviewed distributions, a SHA256 manifest, a deterministic CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM with 7 first-party and 30 runtime components, and a fresh Python 3.14 closed-index wheel installation all passed. The local release-precondition check deliberately refused because it was not a workflow_dispatch from main, while publication readiness deliberately refused without the final dated changelog section, comparison link and docs/releases/v1.0.0.md. A read-only GitHub API check found no v1.0.0 tag and a pypi environment with a required reviewer and branch policy. No package, tag, GitHub Release or protected approval occurred. PEP 740 attestations and live index verification require the authorized workflow; maintainer review remains required. See docs/releases/1.0-publication-rehearsal.md.
